declared_exclusions.item: opal-data-security default encryption is SSE-S3 (AES256) rather than C-8's SSE-KMS on the estate CMK with bucket-key enabled.
declared_exclusions.reason: C-8's key is not a CMK. 86cc6c40-2387-4446-b7e1-de79392e06b3 reads KeyManager=AWS -- the AWS-managed alias/aws/dynamodb service key -- so an S3 bucket cannot specify it, and the account holds no general-purpose customer-managed key (4 CUSTOMER keys, all purpose-specific, over a denominator of 11). Row NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S3. SSE-S3 is the INTERIM ruled by the issuer (msg 19501); the key decision is routed to 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z and the switch is an in-place change in a round-2 cell. NOT a silent substitution: the bound said 'never a new key', and minting one is exactly the decision this seat may not make mid-round.

declared_exclusions.item: The bucket policy's deny-every-principal-outside-an-explicit-list statement is not written this round; only the SecureTransport deny is.
declared_exclusions.reason: Bound (b)'s two named principals do not exist -- 0 of 216 IAM roles match admin|cto|terraform (positive control: 55 match lambda), and the applying principal is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::313476888478:user/Andrew_Berman. Writing the statement against two absent ARNs would deny every principal including the applier, bricking the bucket at creation and requiring account root to clear. Bound (b)'s own rule ('a bucket policy cannot name an absent role') is what defers it. Row NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S4; DEFERRED by issuer ruling 19517 to OP-s-14/15/19, the extenders C-8 already contemplates. The four public-access blocks are the control meanwhile.

declared_exclusions.item: Server access logging to the CloudTrail/access-logs bucket is authored but commented out, not applied.
declared_exclusions.reason: The target opal-cloudtrail-logs-313476888478 permits only cloudtrail.amazonaws.com (bucket policy: two statements, both that service principal) and its ACL holds a single CanonicalUser FULL_CONTROL grant with no LogDelivery group -- so enabling logging requires modifying a bucket this TO does not own, which 'nothing else rides the apply' and never-widen both refuse. The failure mode is the reason it is a stop rather than an attempt: if S3 accepts the config without validating the target, get-bucket-logging would read CONFIGURED while no log is ever delivered, and the specified read observes configuration, never delivery. Row NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S5; DEFERRED by issuer ruling 19532, target question routed to 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z. The resource sits commented in s3.tf with the measurement beside it so landing it later is an uncomment, not a rediscovery.

declared_exclusions.item: The four 7.3 prefixes (cases/, reports/, allowlists/, waf-logs/) are documented as convention rather than created as zero-byte keys.
declared_exclusions.reason: The task order offers both and asks which; this states which and why. S3 has no directories, so a zero-byte key is a real object that would appear in every listing, need its own lifecycle handling, and be indistinguishable from evidence during the fixture cleanup bound (e) requires. The convention is written into s3.tf's header comment.
